name: KMC Speciality Hospitals (India) Ltd
tagline: Small/mid-cap Kauvery-group hospital: the single mature Trichy unit is at 98% occupancy with ~30% EBITDA margins, and a newly-approved Rs 519 Cr / ~591-bed Trichy + Bengaluru expansion finally addresses the 'finite runway' concern - but the payoff is FY28-FY30 and the stock is at ~40x
business_overview: KMC Speciality Hospitals runs a multi-specialty hospital in Trichy (Tiruchirappalli), part of the Kauvery Hospitals group (2,250+ beds across 12 locations). It has an older main facility plus a newer super-specialty/paediatric block; the existing multi-specialty unit is now at ~98% occupancy. In August 2026 the board approved a Rs 519 Cr expansion adding ~591 beds - a ~500-bed / Rs 486 Cr Trichy build (Rs 422 Cr Super-Speciality Block + Rs 64 Cr Mother & Child) plus a 91-bed / Rs 33 Cr Bengaluru Mother & Child hospital - with phased commissioning from Q2 FY28 to Q2 FY30. The unlisted parent, Sri Kauvery Medical Care (India), operates the wider network and plans a separate listing.
fundamentals_table: FY26 ROCE ~20.3% (5-yr avg ~24.4%), ROE ~25%; ROCE dipped below trend and will be pressured further as expansion capex ramps
FY26 revenue Rs 306 Cr (+32%); Q1 FY27 Rs 91.8 Cr (+37.9% YoY, +12% QoQ) - a fourth straight quarter of 33-38% growth
FY26 EBITDA Rs 88-93 Cr, margin ~29.9% (up from 25.6% FY25) on operating leverage + employee-cost ratio falling to ~19.4%. ARPOB +17% YoY to ~Rs 31,481 in Q1 FY27
FY26 PAT Rs 47 Cr (+118%); Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 16.57 Cr (+120% YoY, off a soft base), PBT Rs 22.4 Cr (+124%)
Total debt ~Rs 84 Cr; net-debt/EBITDA ~1.25x; negative working capital (-19 days); FY26 OCF Rs 79 Cr > PAT Rs 47 Cr; net worth Rs 210 Cr. India Ratings IND A+, outlook upgraded to Positive

Rs 519 Cr / ~591 beds approved 14-Aug-2026: Rs 486 Cr Trichy (Rs 422 Cr Super-Speciality + Rs 64 Cr M&C) + Rs 33 Cr / 91-bed Bengaluru M&C. Commissioning Q2 FY28 to Q2 FY30. Funded via internal accruals + term debt
Promoter holding 75% (stable). Corporate guarantee Rs 98.57 Cr to unlisted holding company (SBI loan) - stable, not rising. Zero dividend
fundamentals_narrative: Fundamentally strong and improving: ~20-26% ROCE, negative working capital, OCF consistently above PAT, and FY26 EBITDA margin expanding to ~30% (from 25.6%) as the post-capex fixed base is absorbed and employee-cost ratios fall. The existing multi-specialty unit is now at ~98% occupancy, so near-term growth (FY27) rests on the newer super-specialty/paediatric block ramping and on ARPOB (+17% YoY in Q1 FY27). The material development this pass is the board's approval of a Rs 519 Cr / ~591-bed expansion across Trichy and - for the first time - Bengaluru, funded by internal accruals plus term debt, with commissioning phased Q2 FY28 to Q2 FY30. This directly addresses the long-standing 'single-asset, finite runway' concern, but it is a capex roughly 2.5x net worth, the payoff is 2-4 years out, near-term ROCE will dilute, and the stock already trades at ~40x earnings / ~10.7x book.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Stock ~Rs 138, up ~60% over six months and near cycle highs after a large multi-year run.
sentiment_summary: Read all 46 posts (Jun 2024 to Aug 2026). Trusted user Rahul_Behera (elevated) is the thread's regular tracker, posting each quarter and turning progressively positive - 'excellent result', 'severe operating leverage kicking in', noting Q4 FY26 revenue +35% YoY and margin expansion on flat QoQ revenue driven by lower employee costs. The recurring concerns raised (srinik1988, pskrishnan, rnaveen, Siddharth_Thakor): (1) revenue potential of the old facility is capped, so growth depends entirely on the paediatric/new block; (2) minimal management communication - no commentary on new-hospital ramp; (3) the listed company has extended corporate guarantees to the unlisted parent (~Rs 80 Cr, then ~Rs 98 Cr) and there are related-party transactions with parent-owned hospitals and a medicine-distribution entity, prompting 'is KMC being used to generate profits for the promoter?' questions; (4) peers Kovai Medical and Apollo screen better on some metrics. Rahul_Bhardwaj exited 'in strength' in Feb 2026, willing to re-enter on momentum.
community_signal: Rahul_Behera (trusted, elevated) provides consistent, increasingly positive quarterly coverage focused on the operating-leverage story, without explicit position-sizing language. Balanced against several non-trusted posters' persistent governance/related-party questions and the single-asset limitation. Net: constructive trusted signal, real unresolved governance caveats - though the Rs 519 Cr expansion partly answers the biggest structural objection.
bse_notes: 14-Aug-2026: board approved a Rs 519 Cr / ~591-bed expansion (Trichy Super-Speciality + Mother & Child blocks; a Bengaluru 91-bed Mother & Child hospital), funded via internal accruals + term debt, commissioning Q2 FY28 to Q2 FY30. Land acquired for ~Rs 62.5 Cr (1 acre) for the expansion, explicitly stated not a related-party transaction. Corporate guarantee of Rs 98.57 Cr for the unlisted holding company's (Sri Kauvery Medical Care) SBI loan - stable at the FY26 level. RPTs with parent-owned hospitals and a ~51%-owned medicine-distribution entity ongoing and disclosed. India Ratings: IND A+ affirmed, outlook upgraded to Positive. Parent plans a separate listing. No SEBI action.
